name: Nshima with ifisashi

parts.text: Nshima is a traditional Zambian dish of ground white maize meal boiled with water into a stiff, smooth paste, and maize is considered the country's national staple food. Ifisashi is a mixed dish built on groundnut flour with dark green leafy vegetables and sometimes sweet potatoes, pumpkins, okra or small fish such as kapenta.
Many Zambians eat nshima at two to three daily meals, typically with protein and/or a relish such as ifisashi; thinned into a porridge, it is also given to infants and young children.

blocks.title: Fisashi (vegetables in groundnut sauce)
blocks.sub: One version of the dish, as given by TASTE (Woolworths); the steps are summarised in our own words. Recipes differ from cook to cook.
blocks.note: Covers the ifisashi relish only, not the nshima. This contemporary version by a Zambian cook uses Romaine lettuce as the greens; prep 10 minutes, cooking 30 minutes. T = tablespoon, t = teaspoon.

steps.text: Bring the water, salt and bicarbonate of soda to the boil in a large pan.
Stir in the pounded groundnuts and the tomato and let them cook.
Lower the heat by half, add the sliced lettuce and keep cooking.
Add the onion and cook a little longer, stirring so the groundnuts blend in and the mixture does not catch on the bottom.
Serve with nshima and a protein.
